svg.title: Anti-Corruption Layer
svg.desc: Anti-Corruption Layer. A translation layer that keeps a legacy model from leaking into the new domain. Step 1, The legacy model leaks: No layer: Orders calls the ERP directly, and legacy names and codes creep into its own model. Step 2, Translate at the boundary: The layer takes the call in Orders' terms, calls the ERP its way and translates the reply. Step 3, Legacy changes stop here: The ERP changes a status code: one mapping row is updated, and Orders never notices. Step 4, Keep it thin, then retire: The layer adds a hop and one more thing to run. Once a new service owns customer data, retire it.

g.text: No layer: Orders calls the ERP directly, and legacy names and codes creep into its own model.
The layer takes the call in Orders' terms, calls the ERP its way and translates the reply.
The ERP changes a status code: one mapping row is updated, and Orders never notices.
The layer adds a hop and one more thing to run. Once a new service owns customer data, retire it.
every ERP change can break Orders
the only place that knows both models
+1 hop = extra latency on every call
one mapping row changes, nothing else
one more service to run, scale and monitor
